messages:
Alex M: telemetry-bot alerted high CPU on telemetry-collector-01 — p99 export path is spiking and trace-proxy queue is growing fast. Seeing rising p99 for trace uploads, service incidents start if this keeps up. https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/alerts/telemetry :fire:
Priya R: On it, looking at the dashboard now. Which cluster? collector-01 in us-west-prod? :eyes:
Jon S: If the exporter backlog grows it usually triggers GC spikes on the collector. Do we know which exporter is backing up (bigtable/s3/otlp aggregator)?
Alex M: telemetry-bot shows exporter=otlp-aggregator, queue_length=116k, cpu=91%, p99_export_ms=1420. Full alert payload pasted below.
telemetry-bot: ALERT: collector-cpu-high (collector-01.us-west-prod). metrics: cpu=91, rss_mb=3120, exporter_queue_len=116342, traces_p99_ms=1420. Recent logs: "exporter send failed: backpressure" repeated.
Priya R: Oof. Can we get a heap/GC dump? Also what's our batch processor config now? I think we recently bumped send_batch_size.
Alex M: Dumping current config from the pod: ```yaml
processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 200ms
    send_batch_size: 512
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp]
```
Jon S: 512 is large for us with this traffic profile. Larger batches reduce export ops but increase mem pressure and pause durations when GC hits. For traces the p99 tail latency can blow up. Suggest reduce send_batch_size to 128 and raise timeout to 400ms as a trial.
Sara L: Agreed. Also check retention/eviction policy on the trace-proxy side — if trace-proxy keeps everything in-flight too long we amplify the backlog. We added a callback that retries indefinitely a few weeks ago. Might need to cap retries.
Priya R: Running a quick flame graph on collector-01. Attaching sample top stacks: 
```
java.lang.Thread.run
org.openjdk... GC pause
exporter.OtlpClient.send (blocked on io)
processor.batch.flush (alloc large buffer)
```
Alex M: Nice, confirms blocking exporter send + large buffers. I'm going to patch the deployment with smaller batch size and a bounded retry policy. Rolling patch to 3 pods first.
telemetry-bot: deploy started: telemetry-collector v2.14.1 -> v2.14.1-patch1 on collector-01..03
Jon S: Also consider adding backpressure signals from exporter -> trace-proxy so we can shed non-critical spans earlier. Short term, we should enable span-sampling on ingress for 10% to cut volume while we stabilize.
Priya R: Patch applied to canary pods: send_batch_size=128, timeout=400ms, retry_on_failure.enabled=false. Canary metrics: exporter_queue_len dropped from 110k -> 12k in 3m, cpu dropped 91% -> 42%, p99_export_ms dropped 1420 -> 210.
Sara L: Great. Can we make the retry change more granular (only retry 429/503 up to N times)? We need retries for transient infra errors but not indefinite.
Alex M: Agreed — follow-up PR to add capped exponential backoff for exporter retries and an explicit max_in_flight config for trace-proxy. Creating tickets: INF-432 (capped exporter retries), INF-433 (trace-proxy max_in_flight + backpressure), INF-434 (ingress sampling runbook).
telemetry-bot: deploy succeeded: telemetry-collector canary healthy.
Priya R: Marking incident as mitigated for now. We should schedule a postmortem to look at the change that increased default batch size earlier this quarter.
Alex M: Thanks everyone. Short-term mitigation: reduced batch size + turned off infinite retries + enabled 10% span sampling. Long-term: add backpressure signals, bounded queue, and DR tests for exporter saturation. Follow-up sync at 10:30am tomorrow. :thumbsup:
